components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action a screen exists for: sage fill, graphite label.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid #7c9476; border-radius: 8px; background: #7c9476; color: #15171a; font: 400 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; cursor: default; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #748c6e; border-color: #748c6e; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #71896b; border-color: #71896b; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #475743; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A quiet ink tint over the card; the companion to a primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid #efefef; border-radius: 8px; background: #efefef; color: #333333; font: 400 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; cursor: default; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #e3e3e3; border-color: #e3e3e3; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { background: #d6d6d6; border-color: #d6d6d6; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #475743; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: A rim only; sits beside a primary action without competing.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { height: 28px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.16); border-radius: 8px; background: transparent; color: #333333; font: 400 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; cursor: default; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1), border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.08); } .ds-btn-outline:active { background: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.14); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: #475743; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: 28 pt well with a hairline; the rim darkens on hover and turns accent on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.16); border-radius: 8px; background: #fdfdfd; color: #333333; font: 400 13px/18px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.38); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.36); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #7c9476; }

components.name: Neutral Badge
components.description: Scope and status capsule; the label carries the meaning, the tint only supports it.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.16); border-radius: 9999px; background: #ffffff; color: #333333; font: 500 11px/16px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Card
components.description: A flat white sheet on the page: hairline rim, 12 pt corners, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { padding: 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.16); border-radius: 12px; background: #ffffff; color: #333333; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font: 600 15px/20px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-card-sub { margin: 2px 0 0; font: 400 12px/16px system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; color: rgba(51, 51, 51, 0.55); }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item
components.description: 30 pt row with a 16 pt muted icon; selection is a 12% accent tint, not a filled row.
components.html:

narrative.overview:
CarbonInk 2.0 is an accountant's ledger made digital: a quiet white page, ink-dark figures, hairline rules, and a single accent used only where attention is required. The shell is native — a macOS or Windows window with real traffic lights and native controls — and the interface inside it behaves like a first-class desktop app, not a website in a frame. A consultant scanning a dense screen of activities, factors, and disclosures should feel one thing: everything is in its column, every figure lines up, and nothing is shouting.

Density is a feature here, not a liability: the audience runs many clients against deadlines. The system earns that density by staying quiet — hierarchy comes from type weight, a tight 11–20 pt scale, whitespace rhythm, and 1 pt hairlines rather than color floods, gradients, or chrome. Color appears only as meaning: the accent for the one primary action and the current selection, danger for destructive intent, and the neutral ramp for everything else.

The visual world is built from the platform's own theme: NSGo's neutral palette and system type, with the app contributing its layout grammar, card rhythm, and navigation structure. That keeps light and dark paired by construction — as long as every surface reads its color from the palette instead of freezing a literal.
keyCharacteristics: One white surface for the page and its cards; separation is a 1 pt hairline, never a fill or shadow.
A single moss accent, used on well under a tenth of any screen.
System type at small sizes (11–20 pt), with weight doing the hierarchy work.
Rounded-rectangle cards (12 pt), 16 pt internal padding, generous but regular rhythm.
Native window chrome, native controls, native scrolling; no web-app tells.
Both appearances are first-class: every color comes from the theme palette.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Only one accent exists. It marks the primary action, the current selection, and the focused field — nothing else. A screen with three accent things has no primary action.

rules.name: The Palette-Only Rule
rules.body: Every color is read through `ui.ColorsOf(cx)` inside a `StyleFunc`. A literal color in a static `Style` freezes the light value and breaks the dark appearance; the palette is the source of truth.

rules.name: The Moss Rule
rules.body: Green is the only accent. Moss-500 (`#6b8266`) is the identity color and the selected-row tint. Filled controls use sage (`#7c9476`) with graphite text (5.4:1), stepping to `#748c6e` and `#71896b`; accent-as-text uses moss-700 (`#475743`, 7.5:1). Never put white text on moss-500 (4.2:1) or on sage (3.3:1), and never introduce a second accent.

rules.name: The 13-Point Default Rule
rules.body: Body and control text are 13 pt. 12 pt is for secondary information, 11 pt only for sidebar group labels and badges, 15 pt for titles, and 20 pt for screen headings. Nothing larger belongs in an operational screen.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Figures that change — totals, amounts, CO₂e — use tabular numerals; codes and identifiers use the mono face. Roll-up columns must line up digit for digit.

rules.name: The Inset Shell Rule
rules.body: The window chrome and the page are one continuous surface; the content is a card floating 5 pt above it. Do not paint a second sidebar background, a browser-style toolbar, or a full-width band that breaks the card's silhouette.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Long-form and form content stops at 680–720 pt; data surfaces stop at 980 pt. Full-window line lengths are reserved for tables and the command palette.

rules.name: The No-Fill-For-Elevation Rule
rules.body: A card is never given a gray fill to look raised. If it needs to separate from the page, use the hairline and the corner; if it needs to leave the page, it is a popup and gets the popup's shadow.

dos: Do read every surface color inside a StyleFunc through ui.ColorsOf(cx) so light and dark stay paired.
Do keep the page and its cards on the same white; separate them with the 1 pt hairline and the 12 pt corner.
Do use 13 pt for body and control text, 15 pt for titles, 20 pt for the screen heading, and 11 pt only for sidebar sections and badges.
Do keep 16 pt card padding and the 2/4/6/8/10/12/16 spacing rhythm; use 12 pt gaps inside cards and 16 pt between them.
Do reserve the filled accent button for the one action the screen exists for; pair it with outline or secondary actions.
Do use tabular numerals for quantities and mono for factor codes and IDs.
Do wrap long explanatory copy inside its card; a one-line helper that runs past the card edge is clipped and unreadable.
Do check both zh-CN and en at 640 pt, 1280 pt, and a wide window: CJK labels, unit strings, and factor codes are the overflow cases.
donts: Don't hardcode #fff, #333, or any literal surface color in a static Style; a themed switch will leave the old value behind. Card chrome comes from cardSurface(cx) and only layout stays in the static Style.
Don't add a shadow to a resting card, row, or sidebar to make it "pop".
Don't give a card a gray fill to fake elevation.
Don't use a filled accent row for navigation selection or a colored left stripe as an accent.
Don't add a focus halo, glow, or 2–3 pt ring; shift the border to the accent instead.
Don't uppercase or letter-space section labels; sentence case at 11/600.
Don't put white text on moss-500 #6b8266 (4.2:1) or add a second accent; filled controls use sage #7c9476 with graphite text, and accent-as-text uses moss-700 #475743.
Don't use a gradient, glassmorphism, decorative blur, or a hero-metric block anywhere in the app shell.
